correctness.rationale: The reverse-preimage identity is derived directly from the two transition maps. Monotonicity rigorously allows omission of every nonexpanding inverse b. First useful b creates complement [1,L-1]. Any later useful b follows at least L inverse rotations because shorter shifts leave the missing interval inside the fixed image or crossing zero; every b removes <=k states. This proves universal lower bound 1+ceil((L-1)/k)(L+1). The proposed word shifts the missing interval endpoint forward by exactly k until empty, giving equality for every n>=4,2<=k<=n-2. Independent subset BFS over 78 instances, 2,803,079 finite interval configurations, and 523 larger witness replays passed. Infinite statement depends on symbolic argument, not data extrapolation.

value.rationale: The pair (n,k) specifies a natural infinite family of strongly connected cyclic automata with exactly one nonpermutation letter, whose single action simultaneously collapses k consecutive states. An exact optimal reset threshold and explicit shortest word for every parameter are mathematically more informative than an upper bound or finite table; the k-dependent formula resolves the quantitative cost of rank deficiency, including quadratic-to-linear scaling. The inverse-interval bottleneck is a structural invariant of these automata. The restriction to consecutive sets is mathematically motivated by its nontrivial interval geometry, not an arbitrary numerical slice.
